page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m1.large is a burstable virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, and 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.t6-c1m1.large operates in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance reached 1255.78 and multi-core performance reached 2507.5, both falling into the bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 183.45 GB/sec, but uncached large block read and write speeds drop to 20.37 GB/sec and 15.46 GB/sec respectively. Passmark CPU and memory scores also rank in the bottom 10%, with a database operations score of 616.76 and static web serving throughput of 2.37 GB/sec.

Due to its burstable CPU allocation and low memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is designed for entry-level, low-intensity workloads. The primary tradeoff is the potential for CPU throttling once burst credits are exhausted, combined with limited memory capacity. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile represents a low-cost entry point for non-production environments. It is best suited for lightweight applications such as basic web serving, development and testing environments, code repositories, or microservices with low memory requirements and intermittent CPU utilization.
